items.title: Meta Muse can do your Black Friday shopping at Walmart
items.summary: Walmart will let Meta's Muse shop on its website for users, finding and buying Black Friday deals, via a live Agent Gateway rollout starting November 24.
items.why: Shows retailers opening storefronts to third-party AI shopping agents, which matters for teams building agent commerce integrations and access controls.

items.title: Adding One More Agent: How AI Team Size and Formation Shape Productivity and Diversity in Human-AI Brainstorming Teams
items.summary: A study with 168 participants tested how the number and calibration of AI partners affect human-AI brainstorming, finding two-AI rooms posted more ideas but fewer human-authored ones.
items.why: Suggests adding more AI collaborators can shift output toward AI-authored content, relevant to designing multi-agent team tools.

items.title: Coherence by Construction: Synthesizing CTI Knowledge Graphs and the Formal Limits of Coherence Validation
items.summary: Researchers propose generating knowledge graphs by simulating a process with language-model agents and a deterministic referee, rather than producing objects one at a time.
items.why: Offers a method for keeping relationships between generated structured data coherent, though the text gives limited detail on practical results.

items.title: TOUMAII: A 4.5M-Pair Tool-Calling Preference Dataset and Its Source-Agnostic Generator
items.summary: Researchers released TOUMAII, a 4.5-million-pair tool-calling preference dataset for direct preference optimization, along with a source-agnostic generator.
items.why: Provides a large preference dataset for training enterprise agents to make correct tool calls, useful for fine-tuning pipelines.

items.title: ChatAtom: A Multi-Agent LLM System for Molecular Dynamics Simulation and Visualization
items.summary: ChatAtom is a multi-agent LLM system that turns natural-language requests into complete molecular dynamics workflows, including writing input scripts and analysis.
items.why: Shows LLM agents automating scientific simulation pipelines, a pattern relevant to engineers building domain-specific agent workflows.

items.title: Beyond Final Answers: Interpretable Tumor Immune Microenvironment Reasoning from H&E and mIF
items.summary: Researchers propose interpretable tumor immune microenvironment reasoning by combining H&E tissue images with multiplex immunofluorescence cell phenotypes in multimodal LLMs.
items.why: Highlights the need for step-level verifiable reasoning in multimodal models, though the text offers limited detail on outcomes.

items.title: Memorization and Generalization in Generative Models: A Perspective From Energy-based Modeling and Associative Memory
items.summary: A thesis argues that memorization and generalization can coexist in generative models, framing spurious states in associative memory as a source of creativity.

items.title: Beyond Demographic Discrimination: Benchmarking Normative-Descriptive Calibration in LLMs
items.summary: Researchers introduce normative-descriptive calibration, a benchmark testing whether LLMs treat the same item differently when asked to describe an outcome versus decide one.
items.why: Adds a evaluation dimension beyond demographic fairness, relevant to teams deploying LLMs in socially consequential decisions.

items.title: Towards Robust Partial-Edit Deepfake Localization: An edit and Generator Conditioned Analysis
items.summary: Researchers analyze partial-edit deepfake localization for speech across edit and generator conditions, using WavLM-Large and XLS-R on PartialEdit subsets.
items.why: Shows aggregate detection scores can hide weaknesses across editing conditions, which matters for teams evaluating audio deepfake detectors.

items.title: Budget-Aware Predict-and-Verify Theorem Proving with Heterogeneous LLM Solvers
items.summary: Researchers present BudgetPV, an agentic system that allocates compute across subgoals and heterogeneous LLM theorem solvers based on cost and capability.
items.why: Demonstrates routing subtasks to cheaper or stronger models to balance inference cost against success, a pattern applicable to production model routing.

items.title: AstronautBench: Measuring Agent Self-Improvement Across Episodes Through Knowledge, Evidence, and Progress
items.summary: AstronautBench is a benchmark measuring LLM agent self-improvement across episodes through knowledge, evidence, and task progress views on the same run.
items.why: Argues that task success alone doesn't show learning, offering a multi-view evaluation approach for agent developers.

items.title: Self-Evolving Beyond Human-Crafted Experience for EDA Scripting
items.summary: ZhuLong-SE is an execution-grounded LLM agent that learns reusable knowledge from prior task traces to improve EDA scripting with API retrieval and sandbox execution.
items.why: Shows agents learning from past traces to handle sparsely documented proprietary APIs, relevant to hard-to-document toolchains.

items.title: Self-similar Organization of Information in Language
items.summary: Researchers study how predictive information is carried by preceding text and distributed along history, examining the self-similar organization of information in language.

items.title: CodeReviewBench: An Automated Benchmark for Evaluating the Software Factory
items.summary: CodeReviewBench is a proposed automated benchmark for evaluating AI code review, using PR authors rather than third-party reviewers as the judges of review quality.
items.why: Targets code review as a quality gate for AI-generated code, relevant to teams scaling agent-written pull requests.

items.title: Keep the Process, Change the Supplier: Runtime Governance for Tool-Using AI Agents
items.summary: The Open Process Control Plane (OPCP) is a runtime that mediates tool-using agents' capability calls, recording uncertain outcomes when a supplier may have acted without replying.
items.why: Addresses authorization and audit of agent actions with external side effects, a key concern for production agent governance.

items.title: Right Numbers, Wrong Story: When LLMs Narrate Financial Changes Beyond Their Inputs
items.summary: Researchers show LLM-drafted financial reports can state every number correctly yet add unsupported judgments and causes, appearing far more often than in human-written 10-K filings.
items.why: Accurate figures do not guarantee faithful financial narratives, so teams deploying LLM report drafting need checks beyond numeric accuracy.

items.title: Run One, Get Two: Near-Free Streaming Safety Checks for Local LLMs
items.summary: ToRA is an adapter that runs a second safety-check model as an extra row in the generator's decode step, sharing weights and KV cache for near-free streaming guardrails on local LLMs.
items.why: It offers guard-model accuracy for streaming safety checks without nearly doubling per-token latency on local assistants.

items.title: MixFold: Sub-4-Bit Mixed-Precision LLM Inference via Output-Channel Grouping on Mobile NPUs
items.summary: MixFold proposes executing sub-4-bit mixed-precision LLM weights with native integer operations on mobile NPUs, avoiding conversion to wider datatypes during decoding.
items.why: Memory savings from low-bit quantization only speed up mobile decoding if conversion overhead is avoided, which this method targets.

items.title: From Letter-of-Credit Requirements to Executable Specifications: Evaluating Verification Accuracy and Completeness
items.summary: Researchers propose converting letter-of-credit requirements into executable, atomic checks via a language model and deterministic verifier, evaluated requirement by requirement against gold encodings.
items.why: Checking each requirement rather than only the final decision gives auditable, traceable verification for trade-finance document review.

items.title: Reward Integrity in Adversarial Reinforcement Learning for LLM Guardrail Red-Teaming
items.summary: The paper studies reward fidelity in adversarial RL for red-teaming financial-services LLM guardrails, finding apparent attack wins can come from missing PII or lenient reward judges.
items.why: Reward judges that credit non-successful attacks can mislead guardrail evaluation, so reward signals need verification before trusting results.

items.title: Scalable Evaluation of Medical AI using Evidence-based Practice Recommendations
items.summary: Researchers describe an automated pipeline that extracts clinical criteria and decision trees from practice recommendations to generate medical AI test scenarios across the care continuum.
items.why: Automatically generated, guideline-grounded scenarios could scale evaluation of medical AI beyond costly manual expert benchmark authoring.

items.title: Many Plans at Once: Diverse Top-Quality Planning in Continuous Time
items.summary: Researchers present methods for computing diverse, top-quality plans in continuous time, giving alternative trajectories for physical systems when constraints change.
items.why: Precomputed diverse plans offer ready alternatives and warm starts for robotics and physical planners facing unmodeled constraints.

items.title: Same Facts, Different Decision: Fact-Invariant Manipulation and Provenance-Based Defense in Typed Decision Models
items.summary: The paper introduces LEVER, an attack that uses argumentation-based outside comments to push typed decision models into wrong decisions without adding any new facts, and proposes a provenance-based defense.
items.why: Decision models that consume third-party text can be steered by persuasive comments alone, so input provenance matters for security.

items.title: Integral Multipliers and Arithmetic Obstructions for Two-Hidden-Layer ReLU Maxima
items.summary: The paper derives integer-parameter bounds on the least positive output multiplier for exact representations of six- and seven-input maximum functions by two-hidden-layer ReLU networks.

items.title: Disentangling Verbalized Evaluation Awareness and Refusal through Neuron-Level Intervention
items.summary: Researchers use neuron-level intervention to separate verbalized evaluation awareness from refusal behavior in large reasoning models.
items.why: Understanding whether evaluation awareness drives refusals bears on whether safety tests generalize to deployment behavior.

items.title: Actions Speak Louder than Words: Stateful Privacy Sniffing of LLM Agents via Behavioral Covert Channels in Web Interactions
items.summary: The paper presents a stateful privacy attack in which LLM agents leak private context through behavioral covert channels in their web actions such as searches and link-following.
items.why: Agent actions on the web can reveal private user context even when content filters block direct leakage, expanding the privacy attack surface.

items.title: A Continuous Relaxation of Quantization-Aware Training
items.summary: Researchers propose a continuous relaxation of quantization-aware training to address flat, saddle-point-laden loss surfaces in low-bit, channelwise quantization of large models.
items.why: Sub-2-bit channelwise quantization is hard to train, and a better optimization approach could make hardware-efficient deployment more practical.

items.title: Dynamic Token Merging for Efficient Vision-Language Models
items.summary: The authors extend Dynamic Token Merging, a learned token deletion method, to vision-language models so they can drop visual tokens at inference and reduce cost.
items.why: Removing unneeded visual tokens could cut VLM inference costs when prompts depend on only part of an image.

items.title: Decision Models Are General-Purpose Process Reward Models
items.summary: DM-PRM converts a general-purpose yes/no decision model into a zero-shot process reward model that gives step-level credit without step labels, fine-tuning, or a critic.
items.why: Step-level rewards without labels or critics could simplify RL training for language agents on multi-step tasks.

items.title: Writing Weights or Training Them? Spatial Reasoning through Weight-Space Programming and Low-Rank Adaptation
items.summary: Researchers compare weight-space programming, where one model edits another's weights, with LoRA fine-tuning on spatial reasoning tasks using Qwen3.5-0.8B.
items.why: It compares a gradient-free adaptation method with LoRA on small-model reasoning benchmarks, though the reported gains are modest and task-specific.

items.title: Reasoning in Two Dimensions: Quantifying Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness and Efficiency
items.summary: Researchers propose a framework that represents chain-of-thought as a semantic reasoning graph to measure its faithfulness and efficiency.
items.why: Correct answers alone don't show a model uses its stated reasoning, so this offers a way to audit reasoning traces.

items.title: CoEvoBench: Can LLMs Drive Recursive Co-Evolution of Agentic Systems?
items.summary: Researchers introduce CoEvoBench, a benchmark testing whether LLMs can decide which component of an agent system, model or harness, to change in recursive co-evolution.
items.why: Agent performance depends on both model and harness, so this benchmark targets a joint decision that existing benchmarks leave unmeasured.

items.title: Portable Active Recovery under Timed and Position-Dependent Visual Outages
items.summary: Researchers study quadrotor recovery during camera blackouts, finding hover-and-wait works for timed outages but fails for position-dependent dark zones, which need different responses.
items.why: Drone teams relying on visual navigation without external localization need recovery strategies that distinguish timed from location-based outages.

items.title: When Students Fail to Learn from Teachers: Learning Dynamics of On-Policy Distillation
items.summary: Researchers analyze why on-policy distillation for LLM post-training can be unstable, including a failure mode called spurious agreement that causes repetitive generation.
items.why: Teams using on-policy distillation to post-train LLMs may see length blowups and degradation, so understanding these dynamics matters for training stability.

items.title: MAPES: Multi-Value Alignment Pipeline via Expert Specialization
items.summary: Researchers propose MAPES, a multi-value LLM alignment pipeline that trains value-specific experts in isolated parameter spaces before resolving conflicts.
items.why: Single-signal preference methods can hide conflicts between values, so this approach targets alignment tradeoffs explicitly.

items.title: Double counting in LLM evidence fusion: exact posteriors separate rule compliance from posterior gain
items.summary: Researchers show LLMs can double count shared-source evidence in fusion tasks and build an exact posterior reference to separate rule compliance from real posterior gain.
items.why: Retrieval, multi-agent consensus, and memory systems can overcount correlated reports, so teams need measurable checks on evidence fusion.

items.title: Where Structure Enters a World Model: From Predictive Fit to Physical Rollout
items.summary: Researchers study how adding physical structure, such as conserved quantities and symmetries, to predictive world models affects long-horizon physical coherence.
items.why: Accurate short-term forecasts don't guarantee physically coherent rollouts, which matters for anyone building world models for planning.

items.title: From Acting to Learning: Experience Selection toward Continually Learning Agents
items.summary: Researchers compare nine experience selectors for training a 4B language agent across many seeds and pools to study continual agent learning.
items.why: Choosing which agent experiences to train on affects continual learning results, a practical design decision for agent builders.

items.title: Learning Adaptive Defense Strategies: Fine-Tuned LLMs for Network Security Games under Network Mobility
items.summary: Researchers fine-tune LLMs to act as solver-free surrogates for computing equilibria in honeypot allocation games on networks with changing topology.
items.why: Fine-tuned models could approximate repeated game-theoretic re-solving in security settings, though the abstract gives limited evidence of production readiness.

items.title: What Does Matching a Human Intervention Effect Establish? Benchmark Checks for LLM Simulations
items.summary: Researchers argue that matching a human intervention effect in LLM simulations does not establish validity, using a reanalysis of 70 experiments with GPT-4.
items.why: Teams using LLM simulations as stand-ins for human studies may be overstating validation if they rely on zero-reference equivalence tests.

items.title: EDAGoat: An EDA-Aware Agent for Project-Level GPU Optimization
items.summary: Researchers introduce EDAGoat, an EDA-aware coding agent that optimizes project-level GPU code with optimization patterns and mandatory validation.
items.why: Automating GPU optimization in EDA tools with validation could reduce manual engineering effort while preserving correctness.

items.title: Bel: Step-Level Policy Improvement of Visual Agents Without Training
items.summary: Researchers present Bel, a training-free method that improves visual agent steps by choosing among the agent's own sampled actions using a visual judgment model.
items.why: Teams building screen or robot visual agents may improve step accuracy without retraining, though the abstract gives few benchmark details.

items.title: LiDAR Signals for Robot Locomotion: Spherical Range Images Enable Robust Sim-to-Real Transfer
items.summary: Researchers propose a LiDAR perception pipeline using spherical range images to improve sim-to-real transfer for legged robot locomotion.
items.why: Depth-image and elevation-map approaches suffer sim-to-real gaps, so a LiDAR representation could make locomotion policies more robust on hardware.

items.title: No Perfect Guardrail & No Perfect Guard: On the Decidability of Output Policies for Large Language Models
items.summary: Authors argue LLM output guardrails cannot guarantee safety and present a computational boundary on deciding output policies.
items.why: Teams relying on guardrails as complete safety guarantees should note theoretical limits and keep human responsibility and testing in place.

items.title: DermKG: A Concept-Centric Knowledge Graph for Interpretable Skin Disease Diagnosis from Dermatological Morphology
items.summary: Researchers present DermKG, a concept-centric knowledge graph built on the SkinCon subset of Fitzpatrick17k for interpretable skin disease diagnosis.

items.title: Belief-State Management Meets Rubric Rewards for Agentic Forecasting
items.summary: Researchers propose a forecasting training framework for LLM agents, combining Proactive Belief-State Management in the harness with rubric-based rewards in post-training.
items.why: It targets two known weaknesses of agentic forecasting: context bloat in ReAct loops and slow, noisy outcome-only rewards.

items.title: HookEvo: A Framework for Coordinated Plugin Evolution on Hook-Enabled Agent Runtimes
items.summary: HookEvo is a framework that uses agent runtime lifecycle hooks to evolve task-specific harnesses, with an improver proposing candidates that are evaluated against the current harness.
items.why: It offers a method for automatically repairing tool-using agent failures by coordinating changes to tool receipts, context assembly, and action checks.

items.title: $\gamma$-Scape: An Agent-Centric World for Mobile Embodied Intelligence
items.summary: Researchers introduce γ-Scape, an agent-centric simulation and benchmark platform where agents compose motion tools and learned skills for mobile manipulation tasks.
items.why: It provides a persistent physical simulation benchmark for evaluating embodied agents that combine navigation and manipulation.

items.title: H-MSAE: Hierarchical Sparse Concept Coverage for Efficient and Diverse Instruction Data Selection
items.summary: H-MSAE is a hierarchical sparse instruction selection method that organizes concepts from a Matryoshka sparse autoencoder to pick diverse, compact instruction-tuning subsets.
items.why: It aims to cut instruction-tuning costs by removing semantic redundancy without the annotation overhead of existing diversity selectors.

items.title: GGDriver: Glance at What Is Shared, Gaze at What Differs for Perception-Free Planning
items.summary: GGDriver is an end-to-end driving planner in which each candidate trajectory selects its own visual evidence from camera features to refine and score itself.
items.why: It proposes a per-trajectory attention mechanism for planning, relevant to autonomous driving stack design.

items.title: EcomWriteBench: A Real-World Benchmark for E-commerce Writing Tasks
items.summary: EcomWriteBench is a benchmark of 3,861 queries across 69 e-commerce writing tasks, 13 categories and five languages, for evaluating LLMs on commerce content.
items.why: It offers a domain-specific evaluation set for teams deploying LLMs in e-commerce content and customer workflows.

items.title: GRACE: Controlled Evidence Interventions for Diagnosing and Improving Knowledge Integration in GraphRAG
items.summary: GRACE is a GraphRAG benchmark built from LC-QuAD 2.0 queries over Wikidata, applying controlled evidence interventions to diagnose knowledge integration failures.
items.why: It helps teams tell whether GraphRAG failures come from missing paths, distractors, or conflicts with model knowledge.

items.title: WePM: Hierarchical Conflict Reconciliation for Unified MLLMs
items.summary: WePM proposes hierarchical conflict reconciliation for unified multimodal LLMs, aiming to serve multiple vision-language capabilities within limited on-device memory.
items.why: It addresses running several multimodal capabilities in one model under tight memory and compute budgets on user devices.

items.title: AMARIS: Merging Generalist and Specialist LLMs via Adaptive Subspace Inheritance
items.summary: AMARIS is a training-free model merging method that transfers specialist LLM updates only along selected activation directions to limit interference with general capabilities.
items.why: It offers a training-free alternative to fine-tuning that may preserve broad model abilities when adding domain specialization.

items.title: ReActWAM: Action-Consistent Caching for Efficient World-Action Models
items.summary: ReActWAM is a training-free framework that caches and skips redundant computation in world-action models during consecutive robot inference cycles.
items.why: It could reduce inference overhead for robot policies that generate future visual states alongside actions.

items.title: Evidence sufficiency assessment enables cost-effective review allocation in on-premise clinical AI agents
items.summary: Researchers propose training-free evidence sufficiency assessment and a three-tier triage protocol so an on-premise 4B clinical agent can auto-accept confident diagnoses and defer others.
items.why: It offers a lower-compute way to decide which clinical AI outputs need human review, versus costly repeated-run consistency checks.

items.title: Beyond Linear Decodability: Understanding and Improving Instruction Following in World Action Models
items.summary: Researchers propose linear decodability supervision to improve instruction following in world action models, which often encode target information without acting on it.
items.why: It identifies why robot policies ignore instructions despite encoding the target, and offers a simple training fix.

items.title: Jagged Robustness: Uneven Safety Transfer and Emerging Vulnerabilities under LLM Quantization
items.summary: A study of Qwen3-4B finds that quantization degrades safeguards and bias behavior while truthfulness stays stable, an uneven pattern the authors call Jagged Robustness.
items.why: Teams deploying quantized models should not assume safety behavior transfers evenly; safeguards and bias may degrade.

items.title: Supervaluationism about vagueness and indeterminacy: A judgment-aggregation perspective
items.summary: A philosophy paper examines supervaluationism about vagueness and indeterminacy through the lens of judgment aggregation.

items.title: From Manufacturing Event Logs to Simulation: Enabling SMEs with Agentic AI for SimPy Simulation Generation
items.summary: GenAI4SimPy is a multi-agent framework using the open-weight Qwen 3.6 (27B) model to generate executable SimPy discrete-event simulations from manufacturing event logs, with human validation.
items.why: It shows an open-weight, agent-based route for giving small manufacturers simulation capability without specialized expertise.

items.title: Efficient Natural Language to Temporal Logic Translation for Real-Time Physical AI
items.summary: Researchers study translating natural language into temporal logic for robots using compact models instead of large LLMs, given limited on-device compute and energy.
items.why: Shows how robots could run instruction-to-formal-spec translation on-device, avoiding cloud offloading under tight compute and energy budgets.

items.title: Trained on Harm, Still Refusing: A Training-Time Defense for Code Generation
items.summary: Researchers find fine-tuning on untrusted data can erode code models' refusal of harmful requests, and propose a training-time defense to restore refusal.
items.why: Fine-tuning on untrusted data can silently weaken safety in code models, so teams deploying fine-tuned models need training-time safeguards.

items.title: Altair-Nidhogg: Which Model-Merging Theories Hold for a One-Pass Decision Encoder? Soups, Task Arithmetic, TIES and DARE Against Joint Training and Prediction Ensembling
items.summary: Researchers test whether model-merging methods like weight averaging, task arithmetic, TIES and DARE work for a small one-pass multiple-choice decision model across 156 models.
items.why: Tests whether cheap model merging can replace retraining for adding skills, which matters for maintaining small specialized models.

items.title: Vega-Fafnir: Is Greedy Decoding the Same Decoding? Where Rounding Noise in Speculative Verification Comes From and What Removing It Costs
items.summary: Researchers show that greedy decoding outputs can differ across serving configurations such as batching, padding and speculative decoding due to finite-precision rounding noise.
items.why: Serving optimizations like speculative decoding and padding can change greedy outputs, which matters for reproducibility and evaluation consistency.

items.title: Can Language Models See the Circuit in Pixelated RFIC Passives?
items.summary: Researchers ask whether a frontier language model can understand, predict and edit pixelated inverse-designed RFIC passive structures.
items.why: Tests whether LLMs can help RF engineers interpret and debug unintuitive inverse-designed circuit layouts.

items.title: Benchmarks' Last Exam
items.summary: Researchers review 749 tasks across eight frontier benchmarks and 767 public model evaluations to measure how often task prompts, environments and graders disagree on success.
items.why: Benchmark scores may be distorted by grading defects, so leaders should verify evaluation validity before trusting leaderboard claims.

items.title: Learning Inside Types: Epistemic Typestates for Safe Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Researchers introduce epistemic typestates, a type discipline intended to make multi-agent reinforcement learning agents safe by construction.
items.why: Offers a type-based approach to constraining multi-agent learning agents so safety guarantees hold for any learned policy.

items.title: Learning in Symbiosis: Heterogeneous Federated Learning with ANNs and SNNs
items.summary: Researchers propose heterogeneous federated learning that combines conventional ANNs and spiking neural networks for resource-constrained edge devices.
items.why: Mixing ANN and SNN clients could let energy-efficient edge devices join federated systems without replacing existing architectures.

items.title: Comparative Performance of Machine Learning Architectures for Fault Detection and Diagnosis in Chemical Processes
items.summary: Researchers benchmark multiple machine learning architectures for fault detection and diagnosis on the Tennessee Eastman Process chemical simulation dataset.
items.why: Provides comparative evidence on which ML architectures perform best for industrial process fault detection.

items.title: Spatiotemporal Graph Neural Networks for Fault Detection and Structural Learning in Chemical Processes: Use Case on the Tennessee Eastman Process
items.summary: Researchers propose a spatiotemporal graph neural network that models varying operating conditions for fault detection on the Tennessee Eastman Process.
items.why: Addresses false alarms from legitimate operating-condition changes, a practical problem for industrial monitoring systems.

items.title: Abstract What Varies, Reuse Longer Patterns: Efficient Offline Chain-of-Thought Compression
items.summary: Researchers introduce CRAFT, an offline chain-of-thought compression method that abstracts problem details into slots to reuse longer shared expression templates.
items.why: Reusing shared reasoning templates could cut compressor cost when generating shorter supervision for efficient reasoning models.

items.title: When Are Images Needed in Multimodal Machine Translation? Text-Only Routing for On-Demand Visual Context
items.summary: Researchers propose text-only routing to decide when images are needed in multimodal machine translation, skipping visual encoding when unnecessary.
items.why: Routing before visual encoding could reduce redundant compute in multimodal translation pipelines without losing needed visual context.

items.title: MetaRigor: From Agentic Automation to Verifiable End-to-End Meta-Analysis Through Scientific Decision Boundaries
items.summary: Researchers present MetaRigor, an LLM workflow framework for automated meta-analysis that preserves result identity and applies programmatic verification rules.
items.why: Shows an approach to making LLM-driven evidence extraction verifiable through task contracts and source binding.

items.title: Recoverable Symbols, Unstable Execution: Auditing Internal Pathways and Decision Identity in Visual State Tracking
items.summary: Researchers audit visual state tracking models and find that a model can retain needed symbols yet change answers when irrelevant image content changes.
items.why: Reveals that correct internal features do not guarantee stable decisions, a reliability concern for vision-based systems.

items.title: Average-Depth Variable Execution via Request-Local Token Routing
items.summary: Researchers introduce a method that lets tokens execute variable numbers of Transformer layers, matching each request's mean executed depth to a set budget.
items.why: Per-token layer routing could let inference providers meet request-level compute budgets more precisely than uniform layer skipping.

items.title: Can Vision-Language Models Synthesize Executable Game-Playing Programs?
items.summary: Researchers study whether vision-language models can synthesize executable programs that play games, instead of choosing actions step by step from visual observations.
items.why: It suggests agents could generate reusable game-playing code rather than querying a model at every step, potentially cutting inference costs.

items.title: QuASAR: Toward an LLM-Assisted Framework for Screening, Prototyping, and Assessing Quantum-Advantage Opportunities in Scientific Computing
items.summary: QuASAR is an experimental two-agent LLM pipeline that screens scientific literature for computations that might benefit from quantum algorithms, with a second agent verifying citations.

items.title: A Benchmark Protocol and Fairness Analysis Towards Open-Set EEG Seizure Type Classification
items.summary: Researchers introduce the first open-set recognition protocol for EEG seizure type classification on the Temple University Hospital Seizure Corpus, with a fairness analysis.
items.why: Clinical classifiers that abstain on unfamiliar seizure types may be safer than ones forced to pick a wrong label, which matters for medical ML design.

items.title: ChildAI-Gov: An Evidence-Linked AI System for Assessing EdTech Policies Against Children's Digital Rights
items.summary: ChildAI-Gov is an explainable AI system that scores EdTech policies against children's digital rights using a proposed Child Rights Impact Score across five dimensions.
items.why: Teams building or selling EdTech products may need evidence-linked compliance checks against children's privacy and safety expectations.

items.title: SLP-Bench: Evaluating and Improving Acoustic Claims of Reasoning Audio Language Models on Clinical Speech
items.summary: SLP-Bench is a benchmark that grades each acoustic claim made by reasoning audio language models on clinical speech, checking them against clinicians' perceptual ratings.
items.why: It shows final-answer accuracy can hide unsupported reasoning, so evaluators of reasoning models should check intermediate claims too.

items.title: Auditable Financial Knowledge Graphs: Schema-Driven Construction and Intrinsic Quality Evaluation
items.summary: The paper presents a schema-driven method for building auditable temporal financial knowledge graphs from parsed documents using phased LLM extraction.
items.why: Auditable knowledge graphs offer an alternative to chunk-based RAG for financial documents where temporal facts and traceability matter.

items.title: Beyond Self-Critique: Epistemic Convergence Control for Multi-Agent Research Verification
items.summary: The paper proposes an epistemic convergence control framework for multi-agent research verification, addressing self-critique bias from debating agents built on the same base model.
items.why: Same-model debate agents share latent representations, so adaptive stopping based on convergence may improve verification while reducing wasted compute.

items.title: SLICR: Strategy Logic-Guided Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: SLICR is a specification-guided multi-agent reinforcement learning method that uses Strategy Logic and LTL to shape rewards in adversarial, partially observable settings.

items.title: Integrating Generative Artificial Intelligence with Learning Style Models: Opportunities, Challenges, and Future Directions
items.summary: A PRISMA-guided review of 41 studies examines how generative AI can be integrated with learning style models to support engagement in large online classes.

items.title: Speculative Decoding Is Less Speculative Than You Think
items.summary: The paper introduces DICE, a speculative decoding method that fixes sampling randomness before drafting to better anticipate the target model's path.
items.why: Speculative decoding speedups depend on drafting accuracy, so better candidate selection could improve LLM inference throughput in production.

items.title: The Dual-Tier Sentiment Framework: Scalable Multimodal UX Attribution in Web Search
items.summary: Google researchers describe the Dual-Tier Sentiment Framework, an industrial system that automates UX attribution for large-scale web search using telemetry and multimodal analysis.
items.why: It offers a scalable alternative to slow surveys for evaluating UX during rapid A/B testing in production search systems.

items.title: Functional Depth Is Learned: Isolating the Computation That Layers Produce Only Together
items.summary: The paper introduces an inclusion-exclusion decomposition to track how transformers develop functional depth during pretraining, using public checkpoints such as Pythia.
items.why: Understanding whether layers compute jointly rather than independently informs architecture and pretraining decisions for model depth.

items.title: BioEmu2: Scalable Emulation of Biomolecular Dynamics
items.summary: BioEmu2 is a generative model that predicts atomically resolved biomolecular structures and dynamics, sampling orders of magnitude faster than molecular dynamics.
items.why: Fast generative emulation of molecular dynamics could make large-scale biomolecular simulation practical for drug discovery workflows.

items.title: Grid Cells as Spectral Successor Features: A Reusable Basis for Continual Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: The paper proposes building a successor-feature basis from eigenvectors of a reference policy's transition matrix, inspired by entorhinal grid cells, for continual reinforcement learning.

items.title: VerifiQuant: Governance-by-Execution for Financial LLM Workflows
items.summary: VerifiQuant is a governance-by-execution framework that routes financial LLM queries through an executable diagnostic funnel to answer, clarify, intercept, or refuse.
items.why: Financial teams deploying LLMs need mechanisms to detect when confident numeric answers are unsupported and should not be returned.

items.title: Computing Weighted Set Covers with Heterogeneous Stochastic Oracles: Deadline-Constrained Token Complexity
items.summary: Researchers study a probabilistic Turing machine that selects among heterogeneous AI oracles to solve Weighted Set Cover under deadline and success-probability constraints, analyzing expected token cost.
items.why: It offers a theoretical framework for choosing among LLMs by latency, cost, and capability under deadlines, relevant to cost-aware model routing.

items.title: On the loss landscape of the linear neural network: beyond critical points
items.summary: A paper introduces the critical thalweg, an intermediate structure describing the loss landscape of linear neural networks beyond their critical points.
items.why: It is theoretical work on optimization geometry in linear networks, with limited direct near-term impact for practitioners.

items.title: Model the Annotation, Not the Noise: Semantic Annotation-Channel Prompt Learning against Noisy Labels
items.summary: Researchers propose SACP, a method that models how annotations are generated to improve prompt learning for vision-language models under label noise.
items.why: It addresses label-noise robustness in few-shot prompt tuning of vision-language models, useful for teams training on noisy web data.

items.title: INCISE: Training-Free In-Context Segmentation of Surgical Videos
items.summary: INCISE is a training-free in-context segmentation method for surgical videos that selects reference frames more diversely than random sampling.
items.why: It shows how few annotated references can drive segmentation with a frozen model, reducing expert labeling costs in medical video.

items.title: MomentMem: Memorizing Key Moments for Robot Manipulation
items.summary: MomentMem is a method for robot manipulation that stores key visual moments, evaluated on a new benchmark, VMBench, of long-horizon memory-dependent tasks.
items.why: It targets memory limits in robot policies over long horizons, a practical concern for embodied AI system design.

items.title: Depth-Linked Residual Tokens for Multimodal Retrieval and Generation
items.summary: DepThink introduces Depth-Linked Residual Tokens, learnable tokens for multimodal retrieval and generation that aim to combine single-pass efficiency with sequential refinement.
items.why: It proposes a way to get iterative-style refinement without sequential latency, relevant to efficient multimodal model design.

items.title: Self-verifiable LLM-driven science and why it needs human researchers
items.summary: A paper argues that LLM-driven scientific results need self-verification, comparing it to proof assistants like Lean 4 and Coq, and argues human researchers remain necessary.
items.why: It frames verification cost as the bottleneck for AI-assisted research, a concern for teams relying on model-generated analysis.

items.title: Windchime: an Audiovisual Installation with Audio-Language Model implementations
items.summary: Windchime is an audiovisual installation where spoken prompts are transcribed by ASR, embedded by an audio-language model, and used to retrieve music and animations.
items.why: It is an artistic installation showcasing audio-language retrieval, with limited direct relevance for engineering teams.

items.title: What Helps Language-Model Agents Review Violent Video? A Controlled Comparison with a Human Evidence Reference
items.summary: A controlled study on XD-Violence compares three interfaces for language-model agents that flag violent video: inter-agent messages, a typed evidence format, and a human evidence reference.
items.why: It shows how agent communication design affects accuracy in multi-agent content moderation pipelines.

items.title: MedicalRSI: Medical Recursive Self-Improving Agents via Clinical Model-Harness Co-Evolution
items.summary: MedicalRSI proposes medical LLM agents that recursively self-improve by co-evolving the model and its clinical harness, rather than using a fixed improvement strategy.
items.why: It addresses agents that repeat the same errors after deployment, a key reliability concern for clinical AI systems.

items.title: Search From the Start: Search-Native Pretraining for Language Models
items.summary: Search-Native Pretraining augments pretraining corpora with web-search queries and local-index retrieval so models learn search behavior during pretraining.
items.why: It suggests search skills could be built in at pretraining rather than only in post-training, affecting how tool-using models are trained.

items.title: Realistic Robustness Evaluation of Tabular Data Driven Models
items.summary: AURORA is an open-source modular tool for evaluating the adversarial robustness of machine learning models on tabular data classification.
items.why: It gives teams a tool to test tabular models against adversarial attacks, relevant to high-stakes deployments.

items.title: Rethinking Full-Weight LoRA with Domain and Task Adapter Scaling for Question Answering over Portuguese Well Drilling Reports
items.summary: A study examines how LoRA adapter scaling after training affects question answering over Portuguese well drilling reports using Qwen2.5-7B and Llama models.
items.why: It gives practical evidence that post-training LoRA scaling can be tuned for domain adaptation with scarce data.

items.title: Non-Expanding Gated Continued Fraction Architecture for Feedforward Layers in Language Models
items.summary: Researchers propose a non-expanding gated continued fraction component to replace feedforward layers in language models, aiming for better performance and easier pretraining integration.
items.why: It proposes a parameter-efficient alternative to feedforward layers, though results are early and it remains a research architecture.

items.title: Scoliosis5K: Multimodal Gait Analysis via Clip-Conditioned RGB-Silhouette Fusion
items.summary: Scoliosis5K is a multi-site dataset of 4,998 walking sequences from 3,010 participants, pairing RGB crops, silhouettes, and poses to study scoliosis-related gait classification.

items.title: LoCo-WAM: Test-Time Training as Long Context for World-Action Models
items.summary: Researchers introduce LoCo-WAM, which uses test-time training on newly observed frames to adapt a world-action model's video expert while keeping a short history.
items.why: Offers a way for robot policies to learn from action outcomes within an episode without longer context windows or extra trained models.

items.title: Coherent Moment Propagation: Epistemic Uncertainty for Pre-trained Robot Policies
items.summary: Researchers propose Coherent Moment Propagation, a method for estimating epistemic uncertainty in pre-trained flow matching robot policies at inference time.
items.why: Gives engineers a way to tell when a flow matching robot policy's commands may be untrustworthy in novel situations.

items.title: Your Judge Inherits Your Prompt: In-Context Label Bias in an LLM-as-Judge Is Directional, Not Symmetric
items.summary: A study finds that in-context Yes/No label balance in demonstrations biases an LLM judge used in a video question answering evaluation pipeline, in a directional rather than symmetric way.
items.why: Shows LLM-as-judge scores can drift with prompt example balance, so evaluation pipelines need controls for judge bias.

items.title: ProbeAgent: Principled Diagnosis of Agent Failures in Verifiable Environments
items.summary: ProbeAgent is an automated framework that discovers agent failures in verifiable environments, tests proposed causes, and identifies shared failure modes.
items.why: Provides a systematic method for diagnosing multi-step agent failures beyond inspecting final outputs.

items.title: Modeling Attributional Style at Scale: A Dataset and Analysis for Psychological Attribution Assessment and Reframing
items.summary: Researchers release the Attributional Style Transfer Dataset and evaluation metrics, a benchmark for modeling and reframing attributional style in text.

items.title: Perceive Once, Escalate on Demand: Handing Off Visual KV Memory from Small to Large VLMs
items.summary: Baton proposes handing a small vision-language model's key-value cache over to a large VLM so escalations avoid re-encoding the video history.
items.why: Targets the dominant cost of cascaded VLM escalation in long-video embodied agents, relevant to inference budgets.

items.title: AI-Assisted Decision Support for Formula 1 Pit-Stop Strategy: Deep Reinforcement Learning and Mathematical Programming
items.summary: Researchers build a calibrated Formula 1 pit-stop simulator and compare five deep reinforcement learning agents against a quadratic mixed-integer programming formulation.

items.title: ERA: Embed, Route, Adapt for Cold-Start Cross-Model Latent Retrieval
items.summary: ERA is a system for cold-start cross-model latent retrieval that uses a small anchor budget and a lightweight adapter to avoid re-embedding the whole corpus.
items.why: Could let teams switch query encoders without costly full corpus re-embedding, reducing retrieval migration cost.

items.title: Partially canonical axes in large language model representations
items.summary: Across 12 LLMs from six model families, researchers find native coordinate axes are more aligned with brain responses and interpretable linguistic features than random rotations.

items.title: Tokenize Moments, Not Frames: Tokenizer-Aware Budget Allocation for Training-Free Video LLM Acceleration
items.summary: Researchers propose tokenizer-aware budget allocation that samples video frames to match tokenizer temporal structure, improving training-free acceleration of video LLMs.
items.why: Suggests cheap training-free token pruning for long video can be improved by respecting how the vision tokenizer groups frames.

items.title: SecretAgent: A Multi-Agent Framework for Privacy Protection against Vision Language Models
items.summary: SecretAgent is a multi-agent framework that adds adversarial perturbations to images to protect private information from black-box vision-language models while preserving visual fidelity.
items.why: Offers a privacy-protection approach for shared images that aims to avoid the visible artifacts of prior methods.

items.title: MG-EDA: Maturity-Gated Skew-Normal Estimation of Distribution Algorithms
items.summary: MG-EDA adds a maturity-gated skew-normal correction to estimation of distribution algorithms to help them escape stalls far from the optimum.

items.title: CENTRY: A Probabilistic Latent-State Model for Continual AI Risk Estimation, Monitoring, and Regulation
items.summary: CENTRY proposes a probabilistic latent-state framework for continually estimating, monitoring, and regulating risk of a deployed AI system from its environmental interactions.
items.why: Proposes an implementable runtime risk monitoring model, relevant to teams operating safety-critical deployed AI systems.

items.title: Tracking and Limiting Unsupported Claim Propagation in Multi-Agent LLM Systems: A Provenance-Aware Framework
items.summary: Researchers study how unsupported claims change across multi-agent LLM pipelines and test a provenance-aware framework that passes support status and evidence with each claim.
items.why: Shows provenance metadata may limit unsupported claim drift in multi-agent systems, a reliability concern for agent pipelines.

items.title: Beyond Prompt Heuristics: Assessing Child Safety Alignment in LLMs
items.summary: A study finds six LLMs show considerably higher child-safety misalignment on benign-seeming requests lacking recognizable harm-category cues than on explicit ones.
items.why: Indicates keyword-style safety evaluations may miss child-safety failures, so teams need broader test sets.

items.title: When Perception Collides with Priors: Diagnosing Modal Polarization in Video Understanding Models
items.summary: Researchers identify "Modal Polarization" in multimodal LLMs, where video models either ignore visual evidence for priors or blindly trust video when they conflict.
items.why: Shows video models can fail by over-trusting either priors or perception, a risk for any system that relies on video understanding.

items.title: Contexture: Runtime Context Eviction for High-Throughput Agent Serving
items.summary: Contexture proposes runtime context eviction for LLM agent serving, arguing shared GPU KV cache capacity limits agent throughput and that many earlier tool outputs are superseded.
items.why: Suggests agent serving throughput can be improved by evicting superseded tool-execution context from GPU KV cache.

items.title: Privacy Protection in Self-Evolving Personal Agents: Persistent Memory and Cross-Carrier Transfer
items.summary: A thematic survey examines privacy in self-evolving personal agents with persistent memory, covering memory admission, maintenance, release, and withdrawal.
items.why: Highlights privacy risks of persistent agent memory and the need for controlled memory withdrawal in deployed personal agents.

items.title: JevRisk: Zero-Shot Financial Risk Assessment with a Language Decision Model
items.summary: JevRisk introduces a zero-shot financial risk assessment approach using a language decision model to monitor bank customers for risks like money laundering and credit default.
items.why: Offers a possible alternative to threshold-based and labelled-data risk monitoring in banking, though the description gives limited evaluation detail.

items.title: FoRe: A Force-Guided Framework for Autonomous Grasp Recovery in Vision-Language-Action Models
items.summary: FoRe proposes a force-guided framework enabling vision-language-action robot policies to retry after failed grasps instead of continuing transport.
items.why: Addresses a concrete failure mode in VLA manipulation policies, where robots proceed after a failed grasp instead of retrying.

items.title: Ruby: State-of-the-Art Potency Prediction across Discovery Regimes Using Learned Structural Representations
items.summary: Ruby is a binding affinity predictor for small-molecule drug discovery, claiming state-of-the-art potency prediction across discovery stages using learned structural representations.

items.title: Hypergraph Structural Entropy-Enhanced Hierarchy-Aware Semi-Supervised Graph Classification
items.summary: HypSEE proposes a hypergraph structural entropy-enhanced, hierarchy-aware framework for semi-supervised graph classification.

items.title: Learning 3D MRI Representations with Generative Adversarial Networks
items.summary: Researchers propose learning 3D MRI representations with generative adversarial networks, aiming to avoid slicing volumes and to work better on small datasets than transformers or diffusion models.
items.why: Offers an approach for representation learning on small 3D medical imaging datasets where transformer and diffusion methods struggle.

items.title: PACE: Policy Augmentation and Compensation With Explicit Disturbance Estimation for Robust Locomotion
items.summary: PACE explicitly estimates external disturbances and feeds them into both the policy and controller to improve robust quadrupedal locomotion.
items.why: Suggests explicit disturbance estimation can reduce the tradeoff of domain randomization in learned robot locomotion controllers.

items.title: Weight-space programming and mechanistic interpretability for model editing in particle physics
items.summary: Researchers use sparse autoencoders and mechanistic analysis to edit weights of a particle-physics foundation model, fixing an infrared safety violation caused by pretraining data.
items.why: Demonstrates targeted weight edits and mechanistic interpretability as a way to correct specific flaws in a foundation model.

items.title: Fooling the Mind Twice: Human Detection of Audiovisual Deepfakes Under Repeated Exposure and Corrective Feedback
items.summary: A study of 110 participants finds human audiovisual deepfake detection is unreliable and examines whether repeated exposure with corrective feedback improves judgments.
items.why: Shows humans remain unreliable deepfake detectors, which matters for designing verification workflows that rely on human review.

items.title: Exercised, Rarely Recovered: What Public Reports Say About Recovery in 50 AI Agent Harnesses and Runtimes
items.summary: A study grades 50 AI agent harnesses and runtimes on eight recovery mechanisms, based on public reports about how agents recover from wrong deletions or crashes.
items.why: Suggests recovery mechanisms like checkpoints and rollback are rarely evident in real agent tools, a concern for anyone running coding agents.

items.title: Separating Automation Gains from Agent Contributions in AI-Assisted Model Validation
items.summary: A paper proposes an attribution protocol for LLM agents in bank model validation that credits agents only for faults a deterministic LLM-free workflow does not already find.
items.why: Offers a method to measure true agent contribution versus gains from automation in regulated model validation workflows.

items.title: Epistemic Guard: Out-of-Process MCP Receipt Proxying, Post-Turn Prose Supervision, and Provenance-Gated Memory for Tool-Using Autonomous Agents
items.summary: Epistemic Guard proposes runtime verification for MCP tool-using agents, addressing action fabrication, provenance collapse in memory, and syndicated echo amplification.
items.why: Targets concrete runtime gaps in MCP agents, such as prose narrating failed side effects and unverified content entering durable memory.

items.title: One state, many questions: Opsis gives a frontier model typed eyes for pathology
items.summary: Opsis pairs a frontier model with typed pathology classifiers, reporting that frontier models reading slide descriptions or thumbnails underperform the majority-class baseline on 189 breast report questions.
items.why: Shows frontier models alone underperform on structured pathology questions, pointing to hybrid designs that combine specialist classifiers with LLMs.

items.title: Schema-Validated LLM Workflows: A Benchmark Protocol and Comparative Evaluation Across Six Python Implementations
items.summary: A paper proposes a reproducible benchmark protocol and public artifact comparing six Python LLM workflow frameworks on schema-valid output and task correctness across five business tasks.
items.why: It separates structurally valid LLM output from correct results, helping teams choose frameworks and test LLM outputs at software boundaries.

items.title: Do Senior Agents Do Their Job? Measuring Role Integrity in How LLM Agents Use Subordinate Material
items.summary: Researchers define role integrity and propose measuring whether senior LLM agents truly weigh subordinate agents' reports rather than merely aggregating them.
items.why: Final-answer scores can hide whether a multi-agent orchestrator actually does its job, so teams need process-level evaluation.

items.title: How Does SAM-3 Adapt? Capacity, Update Geometry, and Domain Transfer
items.summary: A study compares five fine-tuning methods for adapting SAM-3 segmentation to medical imaging, remote sensing, and material segmentation datasets.
items.why: Parameter-efficient methods often approach full fine-tuning here, suggesting cheaper adaptation options for specialized vision domains.

items.title: Structure Over Scale: Rethinking Adaptation for Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards
items.summary: Researchers report that LoRA suffers rank collapse under GRPO reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, while a weight-decomposed variant avoids the failure.
items.why: Adapter rank choice can abruptly break RL fine-tuning, so teams using LoRA for RLVR should validate rank settings carefully.

items.title: Co-Evolving Behavioral Agents and Detectors for Adaptive Information Operations
items.summary: IO-AI is a framework that gives simulated information-operation agents engagement and evasion capabilities to test how these affect detector accuracy.
items.why: It offers a way to stress-test detectors against adaptive adversaries rather than only archived, already-removed campaigns.

items.title: Felid: A Flexible and Efficient Design for Transformer Fine-Tuning over Encrypted Data
items.summary: Felid proposes a new ciphertext packing strategy to speed up transformer fine-tuning over fully homomorphic encrypted data.
items.why: Lowering encrypted computation cost could make privacy-preserving LLM fine-tuning on sensitive data more practical.

items.title: GEG-SAM: Gaze Exploration-Guided Segment Anything Model for Weakly Supervised Polyp Segmentation
items.summary: GEG-SAM uses temporally connected endoscopist gaze fixations to guide the Segment Anything Model for weakly supervised polyp segmentation.

items.title: A Frugal AI Framework for India: Responsible and Right-sized AI
items.summary: An IIT Madras CeRAI white paper proposes Responsible Frugal AI as a third path for India, favoring right-sized AI over replicating large foundation-model programmes.
items.why: It offers a policy and design perspective on building AI under tight compute and budget constraints for large, diverse populations.

items.title: DepthMSA: Combinatorial Training and Budget-Aware Depth Allocation for Multimodal Sentiment Analysis
items.summary: DepthMSA proposes combinatorial training and budget-aware depth allocation so multimodal sentiment models process each modality to different depths.
items.why: Allocating compute per modality by predictive benefit could cut inference cost in multimodal models without losing accuracy.

items.title: LingSante-Pulse: Unified Physiological Pretraining through Random-Feature Prediction and Cross-Modal Alignment
items.summary: LingSante-Pulse is a unified physiological representation framework that pretrains a shared encoder on heterogeneous clinical and wearable signals.

items.title: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of Qwen3-VL for Handwritten Mathematical Expression Recognition
items.summary: A study applies rank-16 LoRA to a 4-bit Qwen3-VL-4B model to recognize handwritten math expressions by generating symbol label graphs.
items.why: It shows a compact vision-language model can be adapted to structured recognition tasks under limited compute.

items.title: Explicit Style Extraction for Personalized Long-Form Text Generation
items.summary: StylePrism defines 28 stylistic aspects and SP-Refine makes style extraction an explicit inference-time step for personalized long-form text generation.
items.why: Explicit style extraction offers an alternative to leaving retrieved user texts for the model to interpret implicitly.

items.title: EAF-TTS: Rethinking Codec-Latent Coordinates for Flow TTS
items.summary: EAF-TTS adapts codec latents for flow-based text-to-speech, adding a fixed ZCA interface estimated from training data without learned parameters.

items.title: Neural Defend Ranks #1 in Global Audio Deepfake Detection Benchmark - ARCAS on the Podonos Independent Leaderboard
items.summary: Neural Defend reports its ARCAS models ranked first on the independent Podonos audio deepfake detection leaderboard against commercial and open-source detectors.
items.why: Independent, privately labeled benchmarks offer a more reliable comparison than vendor-internal test results for detection tools.

items.title: Correct Precedents Induce Policy Violations in On-Device LLM Agents
items.summary: Researchers identify a failure where an on-device LLM agent's earlier correct release decisions make it more likely to release a later restricted item, causing violations.
items.why: Local-cloud agents acting as final checks can violate policy even with no faulty steps, so session-level safeguards are needed before irreversible actions.

items.title: NavTTT: Adaptive Parametric Memory via Hierarchical Test-Time Training for Vision-and-Language Navigation
items.summary: Researchers propose NavTTT, a hierarchical test-time training method that gives vision-and-language navigation agents adaptive parametric memory over long streaming observations.
items.why: It targets the finite context limit of transformers for long-horizon embodied agents, a practical bottleneck for navigation systems.

items.title: CreditFilter: Calibrated Token Weights over the Within-Response Entropy Rank for RLVR
items.summary: Researchers introduce CreditFilter, which assigns calibrated per-token weights based on a forking value measuring each token's actual impact on outcome in RLVR training.
items.why: It offers a principled alternative to entropy-based token reweighting heuristics when post-training LLMs with verifiable rewards.

items.title: Proactive Defense Benchmark against Deepfake Generation
items.summary: Researchers present the first unified benchmark for evaluating proactive defenses against deepfake generation across disruption, robustness, and transferability.
items.why: It shows fidelity and identity metrics can conflict, so teams evaluating deepfake defenses should not rely on one metric alone.

items.title: EAGLE: Entity-Aware Grounding with Layered Evidence for High-Resolution Image Understanding
items.summary: Researchers propose EAGLE, a plug-in framework that improves multimodal LLMs' grounding of entities in high-resolution images by selecting reliable signals and layering visual evidence.
items.why: It addresses fine-grained high-resolution image understanding, a known weakness of current multimodal models.

items.title: Preserving Pretrained CFG Structure in RL for Diffusion Models with Conditional Contrast Regularization
items.summary: Researchers propose conditional contrast regularization to preserve pretrained classifier-free guidance structure during reinforcement learning post-training of diffusion models.
items.why: It aims to stop reward gains from degrading overall generation quality, a reward-hacking failure mode in diffusion RL.

items.title: EgoLAM: Learning Latent Actions from Hand and Head Motion
items.summary: Researchers present EgoLAM, which learns latent actions from egocentric video by supervising with measured wrist motion and modeling camera motion separately.
items.why: Separating hand motion from head motion could improve robot policies learned from human video demonstrations.

items.title: Can Reasoning and Image Description Enhance Yes/No Visual Mathematical Understanding?
items.summary: Researchers study whether chain-of-thought reasoning and textual image descriptions improve open-source vision-language models on yes/no visual math questions.
items.why: It gives evidence on when prompting and description aids help VLMs with mathematical images, though the summary offers limited detail on results.

items.title: A Framework for AI-Ready Data in Earth and Environmental Science
items.summary: Researchers present a framework for assessing and improving the AI-readiness of Earth and environmental science datasets, extending FAIR principles to training and deployment needs.
items.why: Teams building ML pipelines on scientific data can use it to check whether datasets meet training and evaluation requirements.

items.title: Do Language Models Know Which Words Steer Their Reasoning?
items.summary: Researchers identify Phantom Context Influence, where language models are steered by semantically irrelevant context words and deny their relevance when asked.
items.why: Irrelevant prompt content can silently skew reasoning, which matters for reliability and auditing of LLM applications.

items.title: Reasoning in Fewer Tokens: Concept-Normalized Multilingual Scratchpads and Reversible Model-Adaptive Reasoning Codes
items.summary: Researchers propose a compression framework that applies Byte-Pair Encoding to reasoning corpora to shorten chain-of-thought traces while keeping them interpretable.
items.why: Shorter reasoning traces could cut inference costs without the lossy trade-offs of discarding tokens or using latent representations.

items.title: Unimodal Shortcuts and Joint Scene-Intent Dependence in Vision-Language Safety Representations
items.summary: Researchers audit five public vision-language safety benchmarks and find each admits a unimodal shortcut, so high scores may not reflect joint scene-intent understanding.
items.why: Benchmark scores can overstate a model's safety reasoning, so teams should check for single-modality shortcuts before trusting results.

items.title: Learning Interaction Dynamics via Motion-Region Guidance for Robotic Video World Models
items.summary: Researchers introduce motion-region guidance to make robotic action-conditioned video world models focus on interaction-relevant regions rather than global reconstruction error.
items.why: Better local interaction fidelity could make video world models more useful for robot policy evaluation and simulation.

items.title: PAVE: A Harness for Geometrically Consistent Road Network Modeling with Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Researchers present PAVE, a harness using vision-language models to build geometrically consistent road network models, reporting OpenStreetMap lane tags correct for only 13 of 44 approaches tested.
items.why: Transportation teams spend significant manual effort building road networks, and automated, consistent alternatives could reduce that work.

items.title: WaXup: Weight Averaging of Experts as Data Augmentation for Robust Introspection
items.summary: Researchers introduce WaXup, which applies weight averaging of finetuned experts as data augmentation to make trainable LLM introspection methods more robust.
items.why: More robust introspection could offer a practical self-diagnostic tool for understanding what finetuning taught a model.

items.title: Testing for Coordination Failures in Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Researchers propose DisQ, a test case selection method that finds failure-revealing states to test cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning policies for safety violations.
items.why: Multi-agent RL policies can violate safety requirements not captured by reward, and DisQ offers a way to surface those failures.

items.title: VMSA: Video Memory Skill Agent for Long Video Understanding
items.summary: Researchers introduce VMSA, a Video Memory Skill Agent that organizes video into external memories and iteratively retrieves evidence for long-video question answering.
items.why: Shows an agentic memory-and-retrieval pattern for reasoning over hours-long video, relevant to teams building long-context multimodal systems.

items.title: PanoUAV-Track: Full-Spherical UAV Visual Tracking in the Wild
items.summary: Researchers present PanoUAV-Track, a benchmark of about 40 hours of 8K panoramic drone video for full-spherical visual object tracking from moving UAVs.
items.why: Provides a new benchmark for omnidirectional drone tracking, highlighting equirectangular projection challenges that standard perspective-camera benchmarks miss.

items.title: Taking Apart and Putting Together: Tracking Objects Through Physical Transformations
items.summary: Researchers introduce Transformation Tracking and Understanding (TTU), extending object tracking to objects that physically assemble and disassemble, maintaining a state graph of relationships.
items.why: Current foundation trackers like SAM 2/3 cannot update semantic identities as objects change physically, a gap relevant to robotics and video perception work.

items.title: Detecting Word-Substitution Poisoning of a RAG Knowledge Base with Relative Entropy and Runtime Verification
items.summary: Researchers show synonym-swap poisoning of a RAG knowledge base lowers answer correctness from 0.714 to 0.555 and study detection using relative entropy and runtime verification.
items.why: Demonstrates a subtle data-integrity threat to RAG systems and a detection approach teams can evaluate for knowledge base monitoring.

items.title: ADEPT: Adaptive Monocular Depth Estimation via Model-In-The-Loop Photometric Tuning with Capture Risk Prediction
items.summary: ADEPT adapts camera exposure and gain for monocular depth estimation using feedback from a frozen depth model and a learned capture-risk predictor.
items.why: Offers a method to tune camera settings for depth estimation on robots, trading light collection against motion blur.

items.title: TrojanMaxxing: One-shotting VLM Backdoors with Weight-Space Programming
items.summary: TrojanMaxxing proposes backdooring vision-language models by using an LLM to directly edit model weights from a natural-language objective, without gradient-based optimization.
items.why: Shows weight-space programming can be misused to implant backdoors in VLMs, a supply-chain security concern for teams deploying third-party models.

items.title: Cleave: Severing Guardrails and Auditing Spectral Coupling in Open-Weight LLMs
items.summary: Cleave is a training-free attack that edits residual writing weights in open-weight LLMs to remove safety guardrails while preserving general capabilities.
items.why: Shows safety refusals in open-weight models can be stripped via weight edits, so teams relying on embedded guardrails for local deployments face real risk.

items.title: Neurodegenerative Differential Diagnosis with Knowledge-enhanced Structural Reasoning
items.summary: KnowSR aligns multimodal patient data with a literature-grounded knowledge bank of disease prototypes to improve differential diagnosis of neurodegenerative disorders.

items.title: No Audio, No Transcripts, No Problem: LLM-based ASR Adaptation Using Only Domain Documents
items.summary: Researchers show a speech recognizer can be adapted to a new domain using only written documents, converted directly or into synthetic spoken dialogs by an LLM, with no audio or transcripts.
items.why: Suggests a low-cost onboarding path for domain-specific ASR when a customer provides only documentation rather than recordings.

items.title: THRIFTY: Cost-Constrained Reasoning-Data Synthesis for Small Language Models
items.summary: THRIFTY proposes cost-constrained synthesis of reasoning data for small language models, allocating teacher-model sampling budget according to query difficulty.
items.why: Targets the major cost of distilling reasoning trajectories from frontier teachers, relevant to teams training small models on a budget.

items.title: Learning When to Ask: Advisor-Aware Post-Training for SLM Agents
items.summary: Researchers post-train small language models to seek advice from a stronger advisor model and act on it, addressing weak multi-step reasoning and tool use in SLM agents.
items.why: Offers a post-training recipe for advisor-executor agent patterns that could make cheap small-model agents more reliable.

items.title: Mechanism Parity for Simulation-Based Validation of Autonomous-Driving Perception
items.summary: The paper proposes mechanism-parity validation, comparing decisive evidence in perception systems across real and synthetic driving scenes to check they use the same evidence.
items.why: Visual realism alone does not show a perception model relies on the same evidence in simulation, a key validity concern for AV testing pipelines.

items.title: On the Challenges of Using LLMs in High-Risk AI Recruitment: Guiding Questions for Legal Conformity with the AI Act
items.summary: The paper presents a toolkit translating EU AI Act obligations for high-risk systems (Articles 9–15, Annex IV) into technical requirements and guiding questions for AI recruitment tools using LLMs.
items.why: Gives engineering teams building LLM-based hiring tools concrete compliance questions to design against AI Act conformity requirements.

items.title: Cecilia: Towards Layout-Inclusive Optical Music Recognition
items.summary: Cecilia introduces a compact representation of MusicXML retaining musical content, lyrics, and layout, and a model that predicts it for optical music recognition.

items.title: ROSWORLD: When Digital Task Competence Meets Physical Execution
items.summary: ROSWorld couples a physically simulated robot workstation to a live OSWorld desktop so a robot and a desktop agent pursue the same tasks under official evaluators.
items.why: Benchmarks whether GUI competence transfers to physical keyboard and mouse execution by robots, relevant to embodied computer-use agents.

items.title: Alignment without Transfer: Tokenization Impacts Cross-lingual Representations during Multilingual Language Model Pretraining
items.summary: Researchers pretrained 39 mono- and bilingual 1B models across five languages, varying only the tokenizer, to study how tokenization shapes cross-lingual representations.
items.why: Shows tokenizer vocabulary allocation affects cross-lingual transfer, a design choice engineers building multilingual models should weigh.

items.title: Learning Unknown Oscillators From Bandit Feedback
items.summary: The paper studies semi-bandit learning with unknown oscillators, where a learner picks two of four reward channels and bounds regret using a confidence-set controller.

items.title: Turnout: Adaptive Attention Switching for Efficient Reasoning
items.summary: Turnout is a method that applies post-hoc linearization to pretrained full-attention models, aiming to recover the accuracy lost on long reasoning tasks while keeping memory savings.
items.why: Targets the accuracy cost of replacing growing KV caches with fixed-size states, relevant to teams serving long-generation reasoning workloads.

items.title: The Assistant Persona Differs Across Languages in Activation Space
items.summary: Researchers extracted the assistant persona direction in 31 languages for Qwen3-32B and found it differs substantially from the English axis, with cosine similarity from 0.378 to 0.911.
items.why: Suggests safety steering vectors extracted from English may not transfer to other languages, a concern for multilingual deployments.

items.title: Self-Supervised Continuous-Time Depth Learning and Ego-Motion Estimation from Asynchronous Events
items.summary: The paper proposes self-supervised continuous-time depth and ego-motion estimation from asynchronous event camera data, assigning each event its own depth.

items.title: PhiJEPA: Denoising Latent Predictions for Visual Representation Learning
items.summary: PhiJEPA is a joint-embedding predictive architecture that adapts two-stage prediction to masked Transformers for visual representation learning from corrupted context.

items.title: PaMuk-Bench: A Parallel Multilingual Multitask Benchmark for Vision-Language Tasks
items.summary: PaMuk-Bench is a parallel multilingual multitask benchmark for vision-language tasks, with over 10K English prompts translated into six languages.
items.why: Provides a parallel evaluation set for measuring VLM performance gaps in lower-resource languages.

items.title: Fix Where It Fails: Root-Cause-Guided Agentic Harness Optimization for Scene Graph Generation
items.summary: RoHa-SGG optimizes the inference harness around a frozen scene graph generation model using root-cause analysis to fix failures without retraining.
items.why: Demonstrates harness-level optimization as a way to improve model performance without retraining, applicable to other agentic pipelines.

items.title: On the Limits of Observability for Evaluating Coverage in Machine Unlearning
items.summary: The paper examines the limits of observability-based evaluation in machine unlearning, using a stress test with 502 retrained models to assess coverage of forget requests.
items.why: Suggests common unlearning evaluations may miss whether a method can fulfill the full range of removal requests.

items.title: Bringing AI Assistance to the Beznau Nuclear Power Plant: A Hierarchical System of LLM Agents for Reactor Monitoring
items.summary: Researchers present a hierarchical multi-agent LLM system to help investigate instrumentation anomalies at Switzerland's Beznau Unit 1 nuclear reactor by unifying siloed data.
items.why: Illustrates a multi-agent LLM deployment in a safety-critical industrial setting with fragmented legacy data sources.

items.title: Unlocking Heterogeneous Accelerator Flexibility in AI Data Centers: Sizing and Workload Allocation
items.summary: The paper proposes jointly sizing and allocating heterogeneous AI accelerators and workloads, such as training, batch, and inference, under limited local grid capacity.
items.why: Frames data center capacity planning around grid constraints and accelerator mix, relevant to infrastructure leads.

items.title: PromptTTSD: Controllable Text to Spoken Dialogue Synthesis with Open-Ended Text Descriptions
items.summary: PromptTTSD is a controllable text-to-spoken-dialogue synthesis method that uses open-ended text descriptions rather than predefined style tags.

items.title: Potential emergence in LLM agents: a statistical physics perspective
items.summary: The paper uses a statistical physics framework, with agent states and a partition function, to study emergence of a global potential governing LLM agent reasoning transitions.

items.title: Hy-MT3: More Accurate, Robust and Practical Multilingual Translation Models in the Wild
items.summary: Tencent's Hy-MT3 is a third-generation multilingual translation model family in 1.8B, 7B, and 30B-A3B MoE sizes, with language coverage expanded from 38 to 102.
items.why: Offers a range of translation model sizes with broader language coverage, useful for teams evaluating self-hosted translation options.

items.title: Embodied-Harness: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Robotic Manipulation
items.summary: Embodied-Harness is a dual-agent framework where an Actor and a Reflector improve VLM-based robotic manipulation by refining the execution harness without updating model weights.
items.why: Shows improving robotic agents through memory and reflection in the harness rather than retraining model parameters.

items.title: Decision Models for Multilingual Emotion Classification: A Comparative Study Against LLMs and Encoders
items.summary: Researchers compare three decision models and two LLMs against fine-tuned encoders for multilingual emotion classification, testing whether zero-shot systems can replace fine-tuning.
items.why: Shows whether closed-answer decision models can match fine-tuned encoders across languages, relevant to choosing low-latency classifiers over LLMs.

items.title: Quantitative Measurement of Pavement Distress based on Vehicle Camera and Perspective Correction
items.summary: Researchers propose a method to measure pavement distress length and area directly from in-vehicle camera images without field camera calibration.

items.title: Shared Understanding in Human-AI Teams: Coordination Continuity in Evolving Work
